title: Amendments
brief: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.

stamps.reason: Its cost is out of proportion: every pinned schema is paid for on every request of every session in exchange for an unmeasured saving of a few ToolSearch round trips, and the card is a counter nobody would mention.
stamps.subject: Regulars

stamps.reason: A variation on what exists: the model of a subagent type is already settable in its agent definition and in the Agent tool's own parameter, earpiece-widget already hooks agent.spawn, and the card is a per-type cost table beside ledger and usage.
stamps.subject: Casting

stamps.reason: Its cost is out of proportion: a model call on every prompt for a three-way classification that will often be wrong, to keep a return address that board-widget and the waiting resume and flow widgets already come close to.
stamps.subject: Yak stack

stamps.reason: A variation on the waiting situation and preflight widgets (project state checked for you), and its own inventor calls it the least surprising: nobody would mention it to a colleague.
stamps.subject: Out of step

stamps.reason: Telling a swallowed sentence from ordinary editing with prompt.edit splices is unreliable, and the card puts on screen exactly the words the person chose not to show; a novelty that wears off after one look.
stamps.subject: Unsent

stamps.reason: A variation on badges-widget and the waiting mirror and wrapped widgets: a phrase counter with a picture, built on a joke that is already everywhere.
stamps.subject: The jar

stamps.reason: Word-shingle overlap with no model will almost never fire on a real repeat and will misfire on boilerplate prompts, so the best moment barely happens; it is also another reader of saved sessions beside ledger and the waiting insight widget.
stamps.subject: Deja vu

stamps.reason: Not chosen: the strongest runner-up, but a transcript row scrolls and a card row is clickable only in the fullscreen layout (the call answers 'none scrolls' elsewhere), so in the default layout it is a list of your own prompts; Amendments works everywhere at no cost.
stamps.subject: Trail

stamps.reason: Amendments reads what no widget has touched (the engine's own system prompt and tool descriptions), shows a changelog nobody publishes, costs no tokens and no cache, and works in every layout.

No blocking fault: every hook and call exists in the 2.1.289 types, all six states and the 20-column card are drawn, demo and live sections present, 118 lines and 15 acceptance lines; 13 notes in spec-notes.md.

Built amendments-widget: captures the engine's shared prompt sections and built-in tool descriptions once per session key, flushes them to amendments.json at turn end, and lists what was added, dropped or rewritten since the version last run, with show [n] for the line diff; 15 acceptance tests and the checker pass.

Nothing is captured when next.trace is absent (own() throws on undefined and the catch swallows it), so the spec's demo path never leaves the working card; at 20 columns wrapped sentences start with a stray space in the empty and unchanged cards; A3 proves the engine path only on the helper. Six findings in inspection.md; the next build needs a fresh live run with --keep.

Fixed all six inspection findings: capture now works when next.trace is absent, sentences are wrapped by the widget so no line starts with a space, A3 raises the widget's own hooks by hand with and without an engine trace entry, show <n> past six digits answers the usage, the age row reads 'since just now' under a minute, and the formatting slip is gone; 15 acceptance tests and the checker pass.

All six findings of the first inspection are fixed: the demo path without next.trace reaches the best-moment card, every state fits 20, 40 and 60 columns with no stray indent, bad files, loose text, big diffs and odd verbs all hold, and the live run took a real baseline of 1 section and 28 tools; five notes in inspection.md.
On the demo page, in the README and the marketplace; smoke test clean
